findings.finding: Recorded argv places -M5120 before --run. The C++ shell parses options up to --run; Shell.lean parses -M into max_memory, then shellMain sets the process-global internal limit in bytes before frontend execution and interpreted main. The equivalent previous argument was -M4096. This source route supports the intended selection but does not directly observe the actual runtime threshold value.
findings.strength: direct source and exact recorded argv

findings.finding: A real override route exists: Shell.lean merges Internal.getOptionOverrides with the override value winning before reading max_memory. The source documents these as build-time stdlib_flags.h overrides. The reviewed packet does not contain the compiled override contents or a runtime threshold dump. No explicit threshold setter or override appears in the active auditor or retained Environment.lean import implementation. It is unsupported to conclude either that the selected -M was ignored or that an override occurred.
findings.strength: direct source possibility; actual override absent from evidence

findings.finding: The auditor retains a reference environment, then imports the full project environment at private level before checking the model/endpoints or printing anything. Retained import code reads serialized/IR parts and constructs large constant/ownership maps. The memory guard samples only periodically, with a source-default 200 calls and a build-overridable frequency. If memory at the same relevant interpreter check is already at or above both limits, both runs can fail at effectively the same phase/time/size despite the 1 GiB threshold increase. This is compatible with the observations, but the packet does not establish that it was the first interpreter check, that either import had completed, or where the exception occurred.
findings.strength: source-supported conditional mechanism; not localized in this run

findings.finding: The auditor passes empty Options to importModules. In the retained Environment.lean function, opts flow to profiling, import finalization and realization context; there is no direct global memory-limit setter. Empty import options alone therefore do not establish a reset of the process-global threshold. Functions outside this retained source slice were not exhaustively traced.

The reported error text matches memory_exception. On the ordinary Linux source branch, the check uses peak self RSS as a fast precheck then current /proc/self/statm RSS; under HAS_JEMALLOC it uses allocator stats. The actual allocator/build flags are not attested. Sampled process-tree RSS and per-process VMS are different metrics and cannot identify the internal counter value. The native shell has a distinct std::bad_alloc error path. No malloc failure, errno, PID-specific allocation, successful import, or successful audit is established.
findings.strength: direct source; build and runtime attribution limited

2429: may use the interpreter and thus is only safe to do after calling `enableInitializersExecution`; see

2434: If `level` is `exported`, the module to be elaborated is assumed to be participating in the module
2435: system and imports will be restricted accordingly. If it is `server`, the data for

2079: private def readModuleDataPartsOfMod (mod : Name) : IO (Array (ModuleData × CompactedRegion)) := do
2080:   let mFile ← findOLean mod
2081:   unless (← mFile.pathExists) do
2082:     throw <| IO.userError s!"object file '{mFile}' of module {mod} does not exist"
2083:   let main ← unsafe CompactedRegion.read (α := ModuleData) mFile #[]
2084:   if !main.1.isModule then
2085:     return #[main]
2086:   -- Opportunistically load all available parts.
2087:   -- Necessary because the import level may be upgraded a later import.
2088:   let sFile := OLeanLevel.server.adjustFileName mFile
2089:   let server ← unsafe CompactedRegion.read (α := ModuleData) sFile #[main.2]
2090:   let pFile := OLeanLevel.private.adjustFileName mFile
2091:   let priv ← unsafe CompactedRegion.read (α := ModuleData) pFile #[main.2, server.2]
2092:   return #[main, server, priv]

2094: private def readIRPartsOfMod (mod : Name) : IO (Array (ModuleData × CompactedRegion)) := do
2095:   let mFile ← findOLean mod
2096:   let irSigFile := mFile.withExtension "ir.sig"
2097:   -- TODO: we don't (necessarily) know whether the module is a `module` or not, but file existence
2098:   -- checks are not great in the face of module-ness changes
2099:   unless (← irSigFile.pathExists) do
2100:     return #[]
2101:   let irSig ← unsafe CompactedRegion.read (α := ModuleData) irSigFile #[]
2102:   -- Opportunistically load all available parts.
2103:   -- Necessary because the import level may be upgraded a later import.
2104:   let irFile := mFile.withExtension "ir"
2105:   let ir ← unsafe CompactedRegion.read (α := ModuleData) irFile #[irSig.2]
2106:   return #[irSig, ir]
